core_obligations: Set up the induction and note the finiteness (proof lines 2543-2550): argue by induction on p, and record that the coverings appearing in Cov are finite, so that all objects of B are quasi-compact in the relevant sense, which is what makes Cech cohomology computable from finitely many terms.

Reduce to a filtered colimit of injectives (proof lines 2553-2602): for a filtered diagram F_i of abelian sheaves, choose functorial injective embeddings to build a filtered system of injective sheaves I_i with a morphism F_i -> I_i, so that the statement is reduced to showing H^p(U, colim I_i) = 0 for p at least 1 and U in B; the author reduces the general case to this one, using the commutativity of filtered colimits with the colimit and the exactness of the functors involved.

Prove the vanishing claim (proof lines 2605-2627): use the vanishing criterion of the same chapter, which requires that Cech cohomology of the colimit with respect to the coverings in Cov vanish; the case p = 0 already proved shows that these Cech complexes are the colimits of the corresponding ones for the F_i, and the criterion then gives the vanishing of the claim and hence the lemma.
proof_roadmap: Induct on the cohomological degree, using that the coverings in Cov are finite.
Replace an arbitrary filtered diagram by one of injective sheaves through functorial injective embeddings, reducing to the vanishing of the cohomology of the colimit.
Apply the vanishing criterion for filtered colimits of injectives, whose hypothesis is exactly that the chosen coverings are cofinal.
Deduce the isomorphism in every degree.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that filtered colimits of abelian sheaves commute with cohomology, uniformly over the objects of a subset B, provided a collection Cov of finite coverings of those objects is cofinal (statement lines 2517-2541). The proof is an induction on the cohomological degree. It first records that finiteness of the coverings in Cov makes the objects of B quasi-compact in the relevant sense (proof lines 2543-2550); then it replaces an arbitrary filtered diagram by one of injective sheaves using functorial injective embeddings, which reduces the statement to the vanishing of H^p on a filtered colimit of injectives (proof lines 2553-2602); finally the vanishing is obtained from the same-chapter criterion for filtered colimits of injective sheaves, whose hypothesis is precisely the cofinality of Cov, with the degree zero case supplying the input (proof lines 2605-2627). The non-formal content is the reduction to the vanishing claim together with the verification that the criterion applies. The claim is H2: a three-step proof, each step written out.
